checks.co_hdc_coverage: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects
checks.co_hdc_public: Doesn't require a Medicaid application first
checks.co_eca_182: No collection lawsuits or garnishment before day 182
checks.co_window_181: Accepts applications for at least 181 days after care
checks.co_window_insured: Insured patients get 45 days after their first post-insurance bill
checks.co_plan_4pct: Payment plans capped at 4% of monthly income, done after 36 payments
checks.fed_window_240: Application window of 240 days after the first bill (501(r))
checks.fed_eca_120: No collection actions in the first 120 days after the first bill (501(r))
checks.monotone: Earning less never means getting less help

policies.headline: If the first bill goes out on day 46 after care (Colorado allows bills from day 46), the policy's written timeline allows collection actions from day 166. Colorado law bars them until day 182.

A household of 3 earning $68,473 a year (250.6% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000 gets no help; the same household earning more, at 251.00% of the poverty line, gets help (amount not stated). The written income bands leave a gap between them.

A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, outside the hospital's service area, uninsured, owing $10,000, after non-emergency care is turned away by this requirement: "must live in an Intermountain service area, unless the care was an emergency". Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.

A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000 meets every requirement, but no rule of this policy grants them help. Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.
